endpoints.description: Service health probe. Reports the resolved state of the two engine modules loaded via dynamic import (media-local, composition-remotion/render), the resolution state of the four media binaries (ffmpeg, ffprobe, whisper-cli, the Whisper model) by logical name and env var — never their resolved host path — and the capabilities enabled in this cycle. Answers 200 in both the ok and degraded states. capabilities gains storyboardQueue in spec-e-burgos-008 cycle-01. The claude CLI is deliberately NOT added to binaries: that list is resolved by @video-maker/media-local and adding it would report degraded on every machine without Claude Code installed, CI included.

responses.405: application/json: { error: { code: 'METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED', stage: null, message, resource, expected } } with an Allow header, for any method other than GET on this path.
responses.500: application/json: { error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', stage: null, message } } from the central error handler.

endpoints.description: Creates a job for the project — render (default), montage or storyboard, selected by an optional kind field in the request body. kind absent, an empty body, or a body without a kind field all mean render, byte for byte identical to before this cycle: no request body was ever read for this endpoint prior to spec-e-burgos-007. render: the stored Timeline is read from work/timeline.json, validated and snapshotted once at creation, so a job always renders the Timeline that existed when it was created and never a later PUT. montage: runs ingestProject then autoMontage from @video-maker/auto-montage over media/<slug>/ with preset (default software-demo) and seed (default 0), rejected with 409 if work/timeline.json already exists unless overwrite: true is sent. The job id is generated by the service; for render it is the same id used for out/<id>.mp4 and work/renders/<id>/. Dispatch is FIFO with concurrency 1 across both kinds: the job is born running when the single slot is free and queued otherwise. storyboard: asks the AI agent (the local claude CLI, no API key) for a storyboard and writes work/storyboard.json. It takes exactly one of brief (an idea to turn into a script) or scriptText (an already written script to split into scenes) — neither or both is STORYBOARD_INPUT_INVALID — and is rejected with 409 if work/storyboard.json already exists unless overwrite: true is sent. Its stages are collect (project inventory: catalog assets, A-roll transcript, previous storyboard), propose (the agent call) and persist. spec-e-burgos-014 cycle-01: montage also accepts scriptPath XOR scriptText (the script the voice reads, used to align the captions word by word against it keeping the whisper timings) and logo: 'auto' | 'off' (default auto: if raw/logo/ has an image it becomes the logo layer of the Timeline, bottom-right). Its report gains logoAssetId and scriptAlignment { replaced, removed, inserted, dropped, corrected }. FIX-e-burgos-008-001: storyboard and voice accept an optional model validated against the PRODUCER_MODELS list of the studio producer, so the chat can run a job with the model of the turn; CLAUDE_CLI_MODEL (default sonnet) is the fallback and the agent is never invoked without --model. FIX-e-burgos-007-001: montage accepts format (the OutputPreset of the Timeline, default reels-9x16) and forwards it to autoMontage as outputPreset. FIX-e-burgos-009-001: voice accepts scriptText XOR scriptPath (one sentence per line) as an alternative to the storyboard, plus gapMs (default 900): it synthesizes one wav per sentence, concatenates them with that silence into work/voice/voice.wav (48 kHz mono), transcribes it into work/voice/voice.words.json and writes work/voice/script-manifest.json with source: 'script'. The job report gains source ('storyboard' | 'script'), a nullable storyboardId and a nullable track { path, wordsPath, durationMs, lineCount, gapMs }. FIX-e-burgos-007-002: montage accepts voice: 'aroll' | 'script' (default 'aroll'). With 'script' the speech source is the track the voice job synthesized (work/voice/voice.wav + work/voice/voice.words.json, described by work/voice/script-manifest.json) instead of the A-roll transcript: concepts, B-roll and captions come from those words, the Timeline voice track points at the wav as an audio asset of its own (kind: 'audio', id work/voice/voice.wav), the A-roll audio is ignored altogether, silence pruning is off (a single keep) and the montage lasts min(voice, A-roll). The report gains voiceSource and a nullable voiceTrack { assetId, durationMs, truncatedMs }. FIX-e-burgos-009-002: kind 'voice' accepts timestamped script lines — [m:ss], [mm:ss] or [m:ss-m:ss] (range separator -, – or —) — mixed freely with unmarked lines. With marks each sentence is placed at its own start (one adelay per segment plus a non-normalizing amix) instead of being chained, and work/voice/script-manifest.json gains four optional per-line fields always written by the pipeline: endMs, requestedStartMs (null without a mark), overflowMs and lengthScale. A sentence that does not fit its window first loses the gapMs cushion, then is re-synthesized with Piper --length-scale down to 0.85 (a 15% limit), and only then displaces the next line, which is recorded as startMs !== requestedStartMs plus overflowMs > 0. schemaVersion stays at 1 and a script with no mark behaves exactly as before. kind 'montage' with voice: 'script' lasts the WHOLE A-roll when the manifest is timed (the narration ends earlier, the tail stays silent, truncatedMs is 0 and the Timeline voice clip is clipped to the wav duration) and keeps min(voice, A-roll) with truncatedMs otherwise. FIX-e-burgos-003-003: kind 'montage' accepts captionStyle — 'bold-impact' | 'clean-sans' | 'outline-pop' | 'subtle-lower' | 'off' — written into timeline.captionStyle and read by the Remotion composition to choose the typographic preset ('off' renders no captions). Absent, the montage preset decides: educational → 'subtle-lower', software-demo/hardware/recipe → 'bold-impact' (the behaviour before the fix). 'subtle-lower' also switches the word grouping to a subtitle (6–10 words per caption over 2–4 s in the lower box). The montage report gains captionStyle, always resolved. When the last timed line declares a range end the track is padded with silence up to it (apad=whole_dur), and a montage over a timed track reports voiceTrack.truncatedMs against the end of the last sentence, never against that padding. A timed script passed to the montage as scriptPath/scriptText is stripped of its marks before the caption alignment, so the brackets never reach a caption.

request_body.schema: { kind?: 'render' | 'montage' | 'storyboard' | 'voice' | 'photo-aroll', preset?: string, seed?: number, overwrite?: boolean, scriptPath?: string, scriptText?: string, logo?: 'auto' | 'off', brief?: string, voice?: string, sceneIds?: string[], gapMs?: number, model?: string, format?: 'reels-9x16' | 'tiktok-9x16' | 'shorts-9x16' | 'youtube-16x9', captionStyle?: 'bold-impact' | 'clean-sans' | 'outline-pop' | 'subtle-lower' | 'off', photos?: string[], output?: string, fps?: 30 } — every field optional; preset/seed/scriptPath/scriptText/logo are read only when kind is 'montage', brief/scriptText only when kind is 'storyboard', sceneIds/gapMs only when kind is 'voice' (and scriptText/scriptPath are read by 'voice' too, as the alternative to the storyboard), overwrite by montage, storyboard and voice, format only when kind is 'montage', and model by storyboard and voice (validated against PRODUCER_MODELS; storyboard passes it to the CLI as --model, voice accepts it for uniformity and ignores it). voice is overloaded by kind: on a 'voice' job it is a voice-model id from GET /voices, on a 'montage' job it is the speech source, 'aroll' (default) or 'script'. captionStyle is read only when kind is 'montage'. photos (required, non-empty array of project-relative paths, each resolved through the producer path resolver and required to sit under raw/images/), output (required, a single portable file name; the target is raw/aroll/<output>) and fps (optional, must be exactly 30 when present, the only supported frame rate) are read only when kind is 'photo-aroll'.

responses.202: application/json: the full Job — { id, kind, slug, state, createdAt, startedAt, finishedAt, progress, report, error } — with a location: /jobs/<id> header. 202 and not 201: the job resource exists and is queryable immediately, the deliverable does not.

responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID for a slug that is not a single kebab-case path segment; JOB_KIND_INVALID when kind is present and neither 'render' nor 'montage'; (kind: render only) TIMELINE_INVALID when the stored document does not parse or validate; (kind: montage only) MONTAGE_PRESET_INVALID, MONTAGE_SEED_INVALID, MONTAGE_OVERWRITE_INVALID for an invalid parameter, or MONTAGE_RAW_MISSING (surfaced when the async job settles, not at request time) when raw/ has no role directory. No job is registered. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }. FIX-e-burgos-009-002: kind 'voice' understands time marks at the start of a script line ([m:ss], [mm:ss], [m:ss-m:ss]) and places that sentence at that time in work/voice/voice.wav, with silence in between; unmarked lines keep chaining with gapMs and a script with no mark is byte-for-byte what it was. script-manifest.json lines gain the optional endMs, requestedStartMs, overflowMs and lengthScale (schemaVersion unchanged at 1, so older manifests still read). spec-e-burgos-017 cycle-01 (TASK-004): fifth job kind 'photo-aroll' builds the Product ad A-roll from photos with no agent-side ffmpeg. Takes photos (raw/images/ paths), output (a raw/aroll/<output> file name) and an optional fps (must be exactly 30). Reads work/voice/script-manifest.json (written by a prior kind: 'voice' job with a script) and builds one Ken Burns clip per manifest line — duration from that line's startMs to the next line's startMs, the last line to the manifest's total durationMs, so every cut lands on a photo change and the total equals the narration; photos cycle when there are fewer than lines and only the first N are used in the given order when there are more. Frames are computed as round(seconds × fps) and used identically as zoompan's d= and ffmpeg's -frames:v, never -t. Clips are concatenated (concat demuxer, -c copy) and the narration (work/voice/voice.wav) is muxed in with the existing EP-006-style mux port. Intermediates live under work/producer/ad/. responses.200: application/json: { slug: string, jobs: [{ id, kind, state, stage, errorCode, createdAt, startedAt, finishedAt }] }. A slug with no jobs answers an empty jobs array, whether or not the project exists.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID for a slug that is not a single kebab-case path segment. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

endpoints.description: Full detail of a single job (render, montage, storyboard, voice or photo-aroll) in any of its six states (queued, running, canceling, succeeded, failed, canceled). responses.200: application/json: the full Job. Also 200 for state: 'failed' — the job's own failure is not a transport error and the typed error is embedded in the body instead of becoming the response status.
responses.404: RENDER_JOB_NOT_FOUND for an id neither the in-memory queue nor the persisted job store knows. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

changelog.change: Adds a kind: 'render' | 'montage' field. For kind: 'montage', progress uses its own stage set (discover/probe/transcribe/plan) and counter field names (processedAssets/totalAssets instead of renderedFrames/totalFrames), and report uses MontageJobReport (catalogPath, timelinePath, editDecisionListPath, preset, seed) instead of RenderPipelineReport. spec-e-burgos-017 cycle-02 (TASK-005): jobs persist in SQLite — every insert, state transition, report and error is written through, and progress is throttled to at most one write per second per job (the last one before a job settles is always flushed). A job still queued, running or canceling when the service restarts is marked failed with error.code JOB_INTERRUPTED at startup, before the server accepts requests. The 404 case no longer mentions a process restart, because a job now survives one; it still fires for a truly unknown id. Every field already published keeps its name, type and meaning.

endpoints.description: Requests cancellation of a job (render or montage). Cancellation is real but cooperative: no process is ever signalled or killed. A queued job is canceled immediately without invoking a single pipeline port. A running job moves to the observable transitional state canceling and settles as canceled at the next stage checkpoint (for montage: only before ingestProject starts or before autoMontage starts — never mid-way through either opaque call), after the binary in flight finishes its current invocation. A job canceled while its last stage is in flight still settles as canceled with report: null even though its on-disk artifacts (out/<jobId>.mp4 for render; work/catalog.json for montage) may already exist and be complete — the entry state wins over the pipeline result. Nothing on disk is ever deleted.

responses.200: application/json: the full Job with state: 'canceled', for a job that was queued. Terminal and done.
responses.202: application/json: the full Job with state: 'canceling', for a job that was running — accepted, still in flight. Repeating the request on an already canceling job answers 202 again, idempotently, and is never a 409.
responses.404: RENDER_JOB_NOT_FOUND for an id the queue does not know. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.409: RENDER_JOB_NOT_CANCELABLE for a job already in a terminal state (succeeded, failed or canceled). Its final state is never changed. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.500: application/json: { error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', stage: null, message } } from the central error handler.

changelog.change: Cancellation now applies with the identical cooperative semantics to kind: 'montage' jobs; no field or status code changes for kind: 'render'.

spec-e-burgos-017 cycle-02 (TASK-005): a job id that only exists in the persisted job store (from a previous run, always in a terminal state after startup recovery) now answers 409 RENDER_JOB_NOT_CANCELABLE instead of 404, matching a job the current process knows about. 404 RENDER_JOB_NOT_FOUND still fires for an id neither the in-memory queue nor the store knows.

endpoints.description: Lists the Piper voice models installed on the machine, each one described well enough to choose it without reading file names. The list is derived from the .onnx files sitting next to the model configured in PIPER_MODEL_PATH, so dropping a new voice in that directory is enough to make it selectable; the .onnx.json config files are not voices and are filtered out, they are read as the metadata of the voice they belong to. It is a resource of its own and not a field of GET /health because health is polled and must not pay a directory read per call. The route is not project-scoped: voices belong to the machine, not to a project.

request_body.schema: Takes no request body.

responses.200: application/json: { voices: [{ id, fileName, isDefault, language: { code, region }, quality, label, description, previewUrl }] } sorted by id. id is the file name without its .onnx extension and is what a voice job accepts in its voice parameter. isDefault marks the model configured in PIPER_MODEL_PATH. language.code is BCP47 (es-AR) and region is null when the model declares none. quality is one of x_low|low|medium|high, taken from the sidecar and otherwise from the file name, and is null when neither declares it. label and description are derived entirely from the model metadata (dataset, language names, audio quality and sample rate) and never state a gender, an age or a temperament, which Piper does not document; without a sidecar the description says so instead of guessing. previewUrl is the path of EP-026 for this voice, relative to the service. An empty array means the directory has no .onnx model.
responses.503: VOICE_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE when PIPER_MODEL_PATH is not set or does not point at a readable file. Answering an empty list there would be a lie: the difference between 'no voices installed' and 'Piper not configured' is what the studio needs to explain. The payload never carries the resolved path of the voice directory. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

endpoints.description: Attaches a locution the user recorded to one scene of the storyboard. The file must already be under raw/voice/ (uploaded with EP-006 and the voice role); this endpoint only names it. The file is normalized to the sample rate of the mix and transcribed with the same Whisper the ingest uses, so an uploaded track carries word timings exactly like a synthesized one, and its entry lands in the manifest with source: 'uploaded' and voiceId: null. A later voice job never replaces an uploaded track, which is how RF-7 is enforced: the recorded locution wins over the synthesized one. The call is synchronous and runs ffmpeg and whisper-cli inline, so a long take holds the connection: turning it into a fourth job kind is a decision left to a future cycle.

request_body.schema: { fileName } where fileName is a portable file name (no separators, no parent segments) already present under raw/voice/ of this project.

responses.200: application/json: { slug, path, track } where path is the project-relative work/voice/manifest.json and track is the VoiceTrack that was stored, with source 'uploaded', voiceId null and the durationMs measured with ffprobe.

endpoints.description: Sends one user message to the producer and starts a turn. The turn runs OUTSIDE the job queue (D-1 of the cycle): the agent enqueues montage/render jobs on this same API and waits for them, so a turn sitting in a queue of concurrency 1 would deadlock itself. Exclusion is per project: one running turn per slug. The user message is persisted before the 202 answers, so the chat can render it immediately. Cancellation kills the child process (it is not the cooperative cancellation of the job queue). The model of the turn is chosen per message: model is optional and validated against PRODUCER_MODELS; when it is absent the service keeps the model of the session and falls back to PRODUCER_MODEL. The model in effect is persisted in session.json, and switching model on a later turn is supported (claude -p --resume <id> --model <m>).

request_body.schema: { text: string, model?: string } — text is the user message, non-empty after trimming; model is one of the aliases of GET .../producer models.allowed. Any other field is ignored.

responses.202: application/json: { slug, turnId, startedAt, status: running }. Poll EP-024 for the events and the answer.
responses.400: REQUEST_BODY_INVALID_JSON when the body is absent, empty or not a JSON object. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND when the project directory does not exist. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.409: PRODUCER_TURN_ACTIVE when the project already has a running turn; resource carries its turnId. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.413: REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE when the body exceeds the JSON body limit. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PRODUCER_MESSAGE_INVALID when text is missing or blank, PRODUCER_MODEL_INVALID when model is present and is not one of the allowed models (resource carries the rejected value, expected the allowed list; the turn is not reserved), PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID when the slug is not a single kebab-case path segment. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.503: PRODUCER_UNAVAILABLE when the Claude Code binary does not resolve or the video-producer skill file cannot be read. Checked before the turn is reserved, so a 503 never leaves the project blocked. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

endpoints.description: Returns the state of one producer turn: its accumulated events while it runs, and its answer plus suggestions when it succeeds. Events are derived from the stream-json output of Claude Code at message granularity (no partial chunks, D-3): a text block becomes a text event, a tool call becomes a tool event with a readable summary built from the command itself, and a failed tool result becomes a status event. The raw stream is kept, one JSON per line, in work/producer/turns/<turnId>.jsonl.

request_body.schema: Takes no request body.

responses.200: application/json: { turnId, slug, status: running|succeeded|failed|canceled, model, startedAt, finishedAt: string|null, events: ({ type: text, text } | { type: tool, name, summary } | { type: status, status })[], assistantMessage: string|null, suggestions: string[], error: ErrorPayload|null }. model is the model the turn actually ran with. assistantMessage is the answer with the ```suggestions block removed; suggestions holds 2 to 4 short actions taken from that block ([] when the model did not emit one). error is filled only when status is failed.
responses.404: PRODUCER_TURN_NOT_FOUND when the turn id is unknown or belongs to another project. The registry lives in memory: a turn from a previous run of the service answers the same 404. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID when the slug is not a single kebab-case path segment. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

changelog.change: Created in spec-e-burgos-015 cycle-01: state, events, answer and suggestions of a producer turn.

endpoints.description: Cancels a running producer turn by killing its child process (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a grace period). Unlike a job, there is no cooperative checkpoint to wait for: the agent is an opaque external process. The answer is 202 because the turn settles when the process actually dies; poll EP-024 until status is canceled. A canceled turn persists neither an assistant message nor a session, so the next turn starts a fresh Claude Code session unless an earlier turn already created one.

request_body.schema: Takes no request body.

responses.202: application/json: the turn record of EP-024, still status running at the moment the kill was requested.
responses.404: PRODUCER_TURN_NOT_FOUND when the turn id is unknown or belongs to another project. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.409: PRODUCER_TURN_NOT_CANCELABLE when the turn already reached succeeded, failed or canceled. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID when the slug is not a single kebab-case path segment. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

endpoints.description: Serves a short spoken demo of one installed Piper voice, so the studio can let the user hear a voice before spending a full narration on it. The phrase is fixed and in Spanish, about four seconds long, and the same for every voice: what is being compared is the timbre, not the text. The first request for a voice synthesizes it with Piper and caches the wav under PIPER_PREVIEW_CACHE_DIR, outside media/ because a demo clip is not material of any project; later requests are served from that cache, and it is rebuilt when the .onnx model is newer than the cached wav. The synthesis runs OUTSIDE the job queue: the queue has concurrency 1 and a preview waiting behind a ten-minute render is not a preview. Two simultaneous requests for the same voice are serialized per voice id, so the wav is synthesized once.
path_params: voiceId — voice model id as published by EP-019 (the .onnx file name without its extension). Only an id present in that catalog is accepted, which is what keeps a crafted path from reaching the filesystem.

request_body.schema: Takes no request body.

responses.200: audio/wav: the demo, streamed, with content-length and Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400. The body is audio, never JSON.
responses.404: VOICE_NOT_FOUND when the id is not in the catalog of EP-019. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
responses.500: VOICE_SYNTHESIS_FAILED when Piper returns without writing a playable wav. The payload never carries the stderr of the process nor the resolved path of the model. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
responses.503: VOICE_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE when PIPER_PATH or PIPER_MODEL_PATH do not resolve on this machine, same condition as EP-019. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.

endpoints.description: Deletes one raw asset of the project. Same path confinement as EP-006: role is one of the six catalog roles and filename a single portable path segment, so the target can never leave raw/<rawDirectoryForRole(role)>/. Removes the file, drops its entry from work/catalog.json (assets, transcripts, ignored and probeFailures alike) and deletes the transcript file the removed transcripts[] entry pointed at — the only derivative the catalog models per asset. Derivatives the catalog does not model (work/renders/<jobId>/, work/edl.json, files under out/) are left orphaned until the next ingest or montage: there is no reverse index tying them to an asset. Serialized per project by the same RenderApiRuntime mutex as the upload, so a delete never interleaves with an upload of the same project. Nothing is removed unless every check passed: a 404, a 409 or a 500 leaves the file and the catalog exactly as they were.

query_params.force: 'true' (the only truthy spelling; any other value is read as absent) deletes an asset the stored timeline still references instead of answering 409.

request_body.schema: Takes no request body.

responses.200: application/json: { slug, deleted: { path, role, catalogEntryRemoved, removedArtifacts }, timelineReferences }. removedArtifacts lists the project-relative paths deleted alongside the asset (the transcript of an aroll asset, if any). timelineReferences is empty on a plain delete and, after ?force=true, carries the uses that were broken: { kind: 'asset' } | { kind: 'clip', track: 'aroll'|'broll'|'voice'|'music', clipId } | { kind: 'logo' }.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND, or ASSET_NOT_FOUND when raw/<dir>/<filename> does not exist in the project. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.409: ASSET_IN_USE — work/timeline.json still references the asset in assets[], in a clip of any track or as logo.assetId. hint carries the comma-separated list of uses (for example 'asset, tracks.aroll clip clip-aroll-1'); retry with ?force=true to delete anyway. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID, ASSET_ROLE_INVALID (expected: 'aroll, broll, image, audio, voice or logo'), ASSET_PATH_INVALID — no storage port was invoked — or TIMELINE_INVALID when work/timeline.json exists but does not validate, because then the references cannot be proven absent. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.500: CATALOG_UNREADABLE with assetPersisted true and catalogUpdated false: the catalog is read before anything is removed, so the asset is still on disk. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

endpoints.description: Lists, recursively, every file the engine produced under exactly three project-relative roots and no other: work/voice, work/producer and out. Read-only and content-blind: it reports path, sizeBytes and modifiedAtMs per file and never parses, streams or deletes anything — the bytes are served by EP-011. It exists so the studio library can show the generated narration, the producer script and the deliverables, which live outside raw/ and therefore never appear in EP-005. A root that does not exist contributes no entries instead of failing.

responses.200: { slug, roots: ['work/voice','work/producer','out'], files: [{ path, sizeBytes, modifiedAtMs }] } — files sorted by root in that order and by name inside each directory, with the files of a subdirectory following its name.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

endpoints.description: Measures a media file already inside the project with ffprobe, so the producer agent (spec-e-burgos-017 cycle-01, tool probe_media) never runs ffprobe itself. The path is resolved through the single producer path resolver (store/producer-writable-paths.ts): it must be project-relative, without '..' or backslashes, and its realpath (symlinks resolved) must stay inside the project root. frames is derived as round(durationMs / 1000 * fps), not read from ffprobe's own nb_frames (frequently absent depending on container); codec falls back to 'unknown' and hasAlpha to false when ffprobe does not report them. video and audio are both null for a still image.

request_body.schema: { path: string } — a non-empty, project-relative path.

responses.200: application/json: { path, durationMs, video: { width, height, fps, frames, codec, hasAlpha } | null, audio: { channels, sampleRate, codec } | null }. Shape frozen as producer_tools STUDIO_TOOLS.probe_media.output in libs/producer-tools.
responses.403: PATH_OUTSIDE_PROJECT when path is absolute, contains '..', uses backslashes, or its realpath resolves outside the project root. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND, or FILE_NOT_FOUND when the resolved path is not a file in the project. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
responses.422: INVALID_INPUT when path is missing, blank or not a string; PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID when the slug is not a single kebab-case path segment. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
responses.500: MEDIA_COMMAND_FAILED, MEDIA_OUTPUT_UNPARSEABLE or MEDIA_BINARY_NOT_FOUND (503) when ffprobe itself fails, translated by translateEngineError. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.

endpoints.description: Extracts up to 12 still JPEG frames from a video already inside the project with ffmpeg (-ss before -i, one 'frames:v 1' call per timestamp), so the producer agent (tool extract_frames) can look at footage without running ffmpeg or reading files itself. Frames are scaled to a 768px long side (short side even, preserving aspect) and written under work/producer/frames/t<ms>.jpg, ms = round(atSeconds * 1000); a repeated timestamp overwrites its own file. The MCP layer (cycle-01 TASK-005) fetches the bytes back through the existing GET /projects/:slug/files/*path.

request_body.schema: { path: string, atSeconds: number[] } — path is project-relative; atSeconds has 1 to 12 non-negative entries (MIN/MAX_EXTRACT_FRAMES_AT_SECONDS of @video-maker/producer-tools).

responses.200: application/json: { frames: [{ atSeconds, path }] }, path project-relative under work/producer/frames/. Shape frozen as producer-tools STUDIO_TOOLS.extract_frames.output.
responses.403: PATH_OUTSIDE_PROJECT when path is absolute, contains '..', uses backslashes, or its realpath resolves outside the project root. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND, or FILE_NOT_FOUND when the source path is not a file in the project. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
responses.422: INVALID_INPUT when path is missing/blank, or atSeconds is not an array of 1 to 12 non-negative numbers; PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID when the slug is not a single kebab-case path segment. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
responses.500: MEDIA_COMMAND_FAILED, MEDIA_OUTPUT_UNPARSEABLE or MEDIA_BINARY_NOT_FOUND (503) when ffmpeg fails on one of the timestamps, translated by translateEngineError. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.

endpoints.description: Copies a file already inside the project to raw/<rawDirectoryForRole(role)>/<filename> for the producer agent (tool copy_asset), replacing the ffmpeg -c copy trick the prompt used to teach. Never deletes the source; refuses to overwrite an existing destination. role and filename reuse the same store/asset-path.ts validation as EP-006/EP-027 (six catalog roles, filename a single portable path segment). Serialized per project through the same uploadSerializer as asset upload/delete so a concurrent copy to the same destination cannot race past the existence check. Does not touch work/catalog.json: a copied asset is picked up by the next ingest or montage the same way any other raw file is.

request_body.schema: { from: string, role: string, filename: string } — from is a non-empty, project-relative path; role is one of aroll, broll, image, audio, voice, logo; filename is a single portable path segment.

responses.403: PATH_OUTSIDE_PROJECT when from is absolute, contains '..', uses backslashes, or its realpath resolves outside the project root. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.

endpoints.description: Searches Wikimedia Commons (generator=search over the File namespace, filetype:audio, formatversion=2) for the producer's search_free_music MCP tool, replacing the old curl-to-Commons shell trick. Calls only https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/api.php with a descriptive User-Agent. Keeps only results whose mime is one of audio/mpeg, audio/wav, audio/x-wav, audio/vnd.wave, audio/flac, audio/x-flac, audio/ogg, audio/opus or application/ogg (Commons reports .ogg/.opus/.oga containers as application/ogg) and whose extmetadata LicenseShortName is CC0, Public domain/PDM, CC BY or CC BY-SA (any version) — CC BY-NC, CC BY-ND and files with no LicenseShortName are dropped. durationMs is required by the contract, so a result with no numeric imageinfo.duration is dropped rather than reported as null. Artist is HTML-stripped into author. resultId is a stable non-cryptographic hash of the File: title. Results are cached in memory per project slug for 1 hour (runtime.musicSearchCache) so EP-035 can resolve a resultId; a fresh search replaces the previous cache entry for that slug. Network failure, a non-200 status or unparseable JSON all become MUSIC_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE — the Commons response body is never included in the error.

query_params.mood: Required. Free text combined server-side into the Commons search as '<mood> filetype:audio'.

request_body.schema: Takes no request body.

responses.200: application/json: { results: [{ resultId, title, durationMs, license, author, pageUrl }] }, at most maxResults entries, license-filtered and mime-filtered. Shape frozen as producer-tools STUDIO_TOOLS.search_free_music.output — downloadUrl is kept server-side only and never leaves this response.
responses.422: INVALID_INPUT when mood is missing/blank or maxResults is missing or outside 1..10; PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID when the slug is not a single kebab-case path segment. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
responses.503: MUSIC_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE when Commons cannot be reached, answers a non-200 status, or returns a body that is not the expected JSON shape. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.

changelog.change: Created in spec-e-burgos-017 cycle-01: server-side Commons search for the producer's search_free_music MCP tool, replacing the shell curl-to-Commons trick.

endpoints.description: Downloads a music result found by EP-034 for the producer's import_music MCP tool. resultId must come from this project's search cache (EP-034), not expired (1h TTL) — otherwise MUSIC_RESULT_UNKNOWN. Downloads only if the file's own url host is exactly upload.wikimedia.org (defense in depth on top of the fact the url was already produced server-side by EP-034), requires a content-length header to enforce the 50 MB cap up front (a response with no content-length is refused rather than streamed unbounded), and writes through the existing upload-temp-then-promote flow (work/.uploads, same as asset upload) into raw/audio/<file name>, where <file name> is the last path segment of the Commons download url; if that name is already taken it is suffixed -2, -3, ... before the source is ever touched, so an import never overwrites an existing file. The whole read-cache/download/promote/write-credit sequence is serialized per project on the same uploadSerializer as asset upload/copy. Appends one entry to work/credits.json (created if missing, existing entries kept; a corrupt existing file is treated as empty rather than blocking the import).

request_body.schema: { resultId: string } — a non-empty resultId returned by a prior GET .../music/search for this same project.

responses.200: application/json: { path, credit: { kind: 'music', path, title, author, license, sourceUrl, importedAt } }. Shape frozen as producer-tools STUDIO_TOOLS.import_music.output — credit is an open record in the contract; this is render-api's own shape for it.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND, or MUSIC_RESULT_UNKNOWN when resultId is not in this project's search cache or its 1h TTL expired. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
responses.422: INVALID_INPUT when resultId is missing or blank; PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID when the slug is not a single kebab-case path segment. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
responses.503: MUSIC_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE when the download host is not upload.wikimedia.org, the response is not 200, content-length is missing or exceeds 50 MB, or the transfer does not complete. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.

changelog.change: Created in spec-e-burgos-017 cycle-01: host-confined download from Commons into raw/audio/ plus a work/credits.json entry, for the producer's import_music MCP tool.

endpoints.description: Retries a job that is failed or canceled by creating a brand new job (a fresh id, retry_of set to the original) with the same kind and the same kind-specific parameters the original job was created with — for kind 'render', the exact Timeline snapshot the original job rendered, never a live re-read of work/timeline.json. Creation reuses the same handler code POST /projects/:slug/jobs runs, so a retry is validated by the exact same preconditions a fresh request of that kind would be (e.g. a montage retry still checks TIMELINE_ALREADY_EXISTS; overwrite is not carried over from the original request, so a retry always behaves like overwrite: false). The original job's own record is never modified: its state, report and error stay exactly as they were.

responses.202: application/json: the full new Job — { id, kind, slug, state, createdAt, startedAt, finishedAt, progress, report, error } — with a location: /jobs/<newId> header. Dispatch follows the same FIFO, concurrency-1 rule as every other job: running if the single slot is free, queued otherwise.
responses.404: RENDER_JOB_NOT_FOUND for an id neither the in-memory queue nor the persisted job store knows, or PROJECT_NOT_FOUND if the original job's project directory is gone. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.409: JOB_NOT_RETRYABLE when the job is not in the failed or canceled state (queued, running, canceling or succeeded); a job that finished successfully is not retryable either, since retrying a good result has no defined meaning. Reusing the creation preconditions can also answer the same 409s POST /projects/:slug/jobs answers for that kind — TIMELINE_ALREADY_EXISTS (render/montage), STORYBOARD_ALREADY_EXISTS (storyboard), VOICE_ALREADY_EXISTS or MONTAGE_VOICE_TRACK_NOT_FOUND (voice/montage/photo-aroll) — if the precondition that held at the original creation no longer holds. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: JOB_RECORD_INVALID when the persisted row cannot be read back as a job of a known kind and state, or its stored params do not pass the same validation POST /projects/:slug/jobs applies to a fresh body — this should only happen to a row written by an incompatible, older version of this service. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.500: application/json: { error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', stage: null, message } } from the central error handler.
